title: TECNO CAMON 50 Ultra 5G Review: Sleek, Durable, and Built to Last
text:
##### Battery life

 

 

 

Coming to the battery life, the phone packs a 6500 mAh (typical) battery. It can easily last for over a day with heavy use and 2 days with typical use, thanks to the optimization. I got over 9 hours of screen-on time with 2 days of use, mostly on Wi-Fi, and occasional 5G use with a smart refresh rate.

 

 

Since the phone has support for 45W fast charging, it can charge up to 50% in about 25 minutes and up to 100% in slightly over an hour, which is decent since the phone packs a large battery. There is reverse wired charging and bypass charging as well when gaming, so the charging current bypasses the battery to go straight to the motherboard, so it doesn’t affect the battery.

##### Conclusion

The TECNO CAMON 50 Ultra 5G stands out as a feature-packed offering in the sub-Rs.40,000 segment. TECNO has focused heavily on areas that matter most for daily usage: a vibrant 144Hz 1.5K AMOLED display, incredible IP68/IP69K water and dust resistance with military-grade durability, feature-rich HiOS 16 software, and a massive 6,500mAh battery housed in an impressively sleek 7.75mm body.

However, the MediaTek Dimensity 7400 Ultimate processor, while smooth for everyday tasks and casual gaming, falls behind dedicated performance-focused competitors in this price range. Similarly, while the main camera and selfie cameras deliver strong results, the telephoto lens offers average performance when pushed beyond moderate zoom levels.

If your priorities are long battery life, a top-tier curved display, supreme build durability, and useful AI software features, the TECNO CAMON 50 Ultra 5G is a solid value choice—especially with the launch coupon and bank discounts.

title: TECNO Camon 50 Ultra 5G: Exceptional Battery and Durability
text:
### Battery and Charging

Battery life may be the Camon 50 Ultra 5G’s best feature, thanks, in part, to that processor and screen resolution.

TECNO fits a 6,500mAh battery into that 7.75mm body, giving the phone far more capacity than many devices of similar thickness.

I checked around and found testing produced an average of around 16 hours for Active Use. Results typically included 24 hours of video playback, 14.5 hours of web browsing, nearly nine hours of gaming, and more than 27 hours of voice calls. Your mileage may vary but I didn’t see anything that would counter these findings.

Real-world battery life depends heavily on screen brightness, network conditions, camera use, and gaming, but those figures point toward a phone that should comfortably handle demanding days.

On paper, charging is less impressive. The included 45W charger reaches roughly 22 percent in 15 minutes and 42 percent in 30 minutes. A complete charge takes around 80 minutes. 

Don’t be misled though, because that’s perfectly usable. Plenty of rivals have pushed well past 45W and buyers coming from phones with 80W, 100W, or faster charging will notice the difference.

TECNO deserves credit for its battery management tools. Users can set a charging limit between 80 and 95 percent, helping reduce long-term battery wear. Bypass charging can power the phone directly during gaming rather than constantly cycling the battery, which can help manage heat.

There is no wireless charging and that’s certainly worth calling out. If you have an arsenal of charging stations, docks, or platters with wireless charging, you might be irked.

...

That leaves the Camon 50 Ultra 5G aimed less at benchmark hunters and more at people who want their phone to last all day, survive rough treatment, take good portraits, and still look like something from a higher price bracket.

...

### Verdict

The TECNO Camon 50 Ultra 5G makes smart choices about where to spend its hardware budget. 

Awarded to products with an average rating of 3.75 stars or higher, the AndroidGuys Smart Pick recognizes a balance of quality, performance, and value. 

Products with this distinction deserve to be on your short list of purchase candidates.

Its 6,500mAh battery is excellent, the curved 1.5K AMOLED panel looks sharp and gets bright, and IP66/IP68/IP69/IP69K protection gives the phone a level of durability rarely seen around this price. The 3x telephoto camera and autofocus selfie camera add useful photographic options.

There are compromises to think about. The Dimensity 7400 Ultimate is more along the lines of competent as opposed to especially powerful. The ultrawide camera is noticeably weaker than the main sensors, and 45W charging feels conservative next to faster rivals. The advertised 144Hz refresh rate is less universal than the specification suggests, too, but 120Hz is still admirable.

Those issues don’t derail the package. And if you’re the target user, you don’t even see the aforementioned things as “issues” anyhow.

...

And with a 6,500mAh battery inside a 7.75mm body, TECNO has pulled off one trick that genuinely deserves attention.

...

4 Score 

The TECNO Camon 50 Ultra 5G delivers excellent battery life, serious durability, a sharp 1.5K AMOLED display, and a useful 3x telephoto camera at a price that lands around $400 in many markets. Its Dimensity 7400 Ultimate processor is plenty capable for everyday use, though demanding gamers will find faster options elsewhere. Slower 45W charging, no wireless charging, and a modest ultrawide camera are the clearest compromises. For buyers who value endurance, cameras, and durability ahead of raw performance, TECNO has put together a very sensible package.

title: TECNO CAMON 50 Ultra 5G First Impressions: A Great Makeover
text:
Initial verdict: The CAMON 50 Ultra 5G is a good follow-up to last year’s CAMON 40 Pro 5G with the inclusion of a telephoto camera and a UI overall.

#### Pros

- Now has a telephoto camera
- Decent battery life
- Has eSIM support

#### Cons

...

The CAMON 50 Ultra 5G uses a Dimensity 7400 processor, and is paired with 8GB RAM and 256GB UFS 2.2 storage. While we wished TECNO used UFS 3.1 storage, it’s a necessary compromise as an effect of the RAMpocalypse.

The Dimensity 7400 is technically similar to the Dimensity 7300 used on the CAMON 40 Pro 5G, but you’re getting a better GPU. This allows the CAMON 50 Ultra 5G to run demanding mobile games better and offer better image processing.

The CAMON 50 Ultra 5G comes with HiOS 16 out of the box, and TECNO promises three Android updates and 5 years of security updates. Bloatware is kept to a minimum (most of them can be uninstalled), and the overall experience feels smoother compared to previous HiOS iterations.

TECNO’s Ella AI has a comprehensive set of AI features that include video generation, theme generator, and document summarization. There’s also a health measuring tool that scans your face to give you readings on your heart rate and blood oxygen. It’s one of the more unique AI features we’ve seen on a phone, and to TECNO’s credit, the readings we got are close to what you get with a fitness tracker.

A major change for the CAMON 50 Ultra 5G is its battery capacity: while only 0.1mm thicker than the CAMON 40 Pro 5G, TECNO managed to stuff a 6500mAh battery inside. That’s a good 20% increase while keeping the phone still slim. Battery life is respectable too: we got 16 hours in PCMark’s battery benchmark, which translates of being able to use the CAMON 50 Ultra 5G for around 1.5 days on a single charge.

...

Despite the challenges caused by the RAMpocalypse, the CAMON 50 Ultra 5G appears to be a promising and solid follow up to last year’s CAMON 40 Pro 5G especially with the inclusion of eSIM, a telephoto camera, and a better software experience. The biggest question here is how much TECNO will price it in the Philippines–we think if they manage to keep it within the Php 20,000 range, the CAMON 50 Ultra 5G might be the most well-rounded midrange phone for its price point.

text:
## Battery and Charging

If there's one area where the CAMON 50 Ultra 5G consistently impressed me, it's battery life. Despite its slim 7.75mm profile and lightweight 181g body, TECNO managed to fit a massive 6500mAh battery inside.

In everyday use, battery life was excellent. My typical routine of taking photos, uploading content, browsing social media, replying to messages, streaming videos, and occasional gaming was enough to comfortably get through a full day with plenty of charge remaining. Users with lighter workloads can even expect more than two days of use on a single charge.

 Charging is handled by a 45W Super Charge adapter. Because of the large battery capacity, a full charge takes around 1 hour and 30 minutes from empty. While it isn't the fastest charging system available today, a quick 15-minute top-up can recover roughly 25% to 30% of battery life, which is often enough for several more hours of use.

TECNO also includes Bypass Charging, which routes power directly to the phone during gaming rather than continuously charging the battery. This helps reduce heat and may contribute to better long-term battery health during extended gaming sessions.

 Speaking of longevity, TECNO rates the battery for up to 1,800 charging cycles while retaining over 80% of its original capacity, offering better long-term durability than many conventional smartphone batteries.

 The only notable omission is wireless charging. Overall, the CAMON 50 Ultra 5G delivers excellent battery endurance, practical charging speeds, and useful battery management features, making it a dependable device for heavy users and content creators alike.

...

After spending several weeks with the CAMON 50 Ultra 5G, it left a positive impression as a smartphone that consistently delivered where it mattered most. It combines a premium design, excellent battery life, a vibrant 144Hz AMOLED display, dependable performance, and a versatile camera system into a package that feels polished and practical for everyday use.

 What impressed me most is that no single feature carries the entire experience. The cameras are dependable, the display is excellent, battery life is outstanding, and the overall software experience feels more refined than previous CAMON devices. The addition of IP66, IP68, and IP69K ratings, a dedicated telephoto camera, and useful features like Bypass Charging help the phone stand out in an increasingly competitive segment.

 It's not without compromises. The ultra-wide camera isn't quite on the same level as the main and telephoto cameras, there's no eSIM or wireless charging support, and a few pre-installed apps still come with the system.

##### TECNO CAMON 50 Ultra 5G Review: Battery

Battery life is easily one of the strongest selling points of the CAMON 50 Ultra 5G.

Its 6,500mAh battery provides excellent endurance that comfortably lasts through a full day of heavy use. During our review, the phone handled hours of photography, video streaming, messaging, and social media browsing without requiring a mid-day charge.

For users upgrading from older devices with aging batteries, this alone can feel like a significant quality-of-life improvement.

Charging speeds are equally practical. The included 45W fast charging isn’t the fastest available today, but it strikes a reasonable balance considering the battery’s large capacity.

More importantly, you’ll spend less time worrying about charging because the phone simply lasts longer between top-ups.

##### Verdict

The TECNO CAMON 50 Ultra 5G succeeds because it understands what most smartphone buyers actually want.

Not everyone needs flagship-level performance. Most users simply want a phone that takes good photos, lasts all day, runs smoothly, and feels reliable for several years. That’s exactly where the CAMON 50 Ultra 5G delivers.

The telephoto camera adds genuine versatility, the AMOLED display is excellent for media consumption, performance is dependable for everyday use, and the massive battery provides outstanding endurance. Add the impressive durability ratings, and the overall package becomes even more attractive.
